title: CTS 2026 Weekly Survey 2 - Pornography and the Church

field_dates.final_close_rule: 20 days after the first production invitation send

suggestion_columns: Suggest one or more future CTS survey items. Please write each suggestion as a statement that a participant could rate from 0 to 100.

source_columns: Which of these participant-nominated survey items would you most like to see considered for next week's live survey items? Move the items up or down to indicate your preference. These ballot items are intentionally independent from this week's Pornography and the Church topic. CTS reviews participant suggestions with AI assistance, polishing them for clarity, neutrality, survey suitability, and likely participant tension.
choices: Christians are morally obligated to disobey civil laws that require them to violate clear biblical commands.
Churches should teach explicitly on the moral and pastoral implications of IVF and other assisted reproductive technologies.
Women should be permitted to serve in any church ministry role for which they are spiritually gifted and otherwise qualified.
Baptism should ordinarily precede participation in the Lord's Supper.
Churches should teach Christians how to use artificial intelligence faithfully and critically as part of contemporary discipleship.

items.text: Churches should explicitly teach regular attenders that committed local church membership is a normal part of Christian discipleship.
Churches should prioritize faithful Christian witness over gaining political power as their primary public posture.
Churches should prioritize communities of connection and service over programs aimed mainly at individual spiritual growth.
Scripture reserves the office of pastor or elder for qualified men.
A complementarian church should treat a pastoral candidate's egalitarian convictions as disqualifying for its senior pastor role.

report_encapsulation.title: Week 2 refreshed preliminary report: Pornography and the Church
report_encapsulation.text: The refreshed Week 2 preliminary report has 36 complete responses. Current patterns show high agreement around pornography's prevalence among Christian men, pastoral accountability for persistent pornography use, direct leadership screening, pastoral care for harmed spouses, and proactive youth teaching, with wider spread around accountability software, marijuana avoidance, and whether churches are losing more ground than they are gaining. Raw respondent identities and raw free-text suggestions are not published.
